name: Anthropic
profile:
# Anthropic (Claude) — Hackathon Builder Profile

## Capabilities and APIs you can use in a weekend
- **Messages API**: direct model prompting for custom agent loops and fine-grained control.
- **Claude Managed Agents**: pre-built agent harness for **long-running tasks** and **asynchronous work**.
- **Core model features**: text + image input, text output, multilingual support, vision, and tool use.
- **Useful build primitives**: structured outputs, streaming messages, batch processing, citations, embeddings, prompt caching, context editing, message threads, compaction, and files/PDF support.
- **Tooling**: web search/fetch, code execution, bash, browser/computer use, memory, text editor, MCP connectors/remote MCP servers, and skills.

## Hero use cases the docs showcase
- **Research** and **knowledge work**
- **Coding** and **agentic coding**
- **Long-horizon agentic tasks**
- **Writing**
- **Classification, extraction, and routing** for high-volume/low-latency workflows
- General **analysis** and **reasoning**

## What it rewards in hackathon projects
The docs don’t describe hackathon judging criteria, but they strongly emphasize:
- **Good model selection** for the workload
- **Agentic workflows** with tool use and orchestration
- **Long-running, async experiences**
- **Structured outputs** and **citations** for reliability
- Efficient use of **context management** and **prompt caching**
- Handling **stop reasons**, **refusals**, and fallback paths gracefully

## Recent or notable features worth building on now
- **Latest model lineup**:
  - **Fable 5.1**: most capable; built for **research** and **multi-day tasks**
  - **Opus 5.5**: for **complex projects**, **agents**, and **coding**
  - **Sonnet 5.5**: balanced speed/intelligence for everyday tasks
  - **Haiku 5.5**: fastest and lowest cost for high-volume tasks
- **All current models** support text/image input, multilingual capability, vision, and tool use.
- The docs highlight **effort**, **fast mode**, **task budgets (beta)**, and **streaming refusals** as notable controls/features for production-like behavior.

prior_art.excerpt: ## Inspiration Through cold DMs, LinkedIn, and founder networks, we reached out to several Large Language Model (LLM) startup founders. We found a shared issue: there was no extremely extremely easy solution for monitoring their LLM in real-life applications. Most founders didn't find existing LLM monitoring solutions braindead easy to set up and were still sifting through chat logs and making manual adjustments every day. Our simple goal was to reduce this wasted time by create an extremely simple solution focused on significantly reducing manual monitoring time. ## What it does Drift is a library that wraps around standard OpenAI/Anthropic LLM calls. It allows users to compare LLM responses with custom-defined target phrases. prior_art.title: TestudoSync
prior_art.excerpt: ## Inspiration Every semester, UMD students waste 30+ minutes manually entering class schedules into their calendars. We thought: there has to be a better way. One click should be enough. ## What it does A browser extension that scrapes your Testudo schedule and instantly converts it to a downloadable ICS calendar file. Works with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook—anywhere, for the entire schedule. ## How we built it Pure JavaScript browser extension with DOM scraping, ICS format generation, and Chrome APIs. We built a text-based fallback parser for Testudo's Angular interface, added comprehensive error handling, and created a standalone HTML version as backup. Built and deployed in under 45 minutes. ## Challenges we ran into Testudo's Angular-based interface was tricky—dynamic content loading and inconsistent class names made DOM scraping unpredictable.
